inputs.name: jellyfin_version
inputs.description: Jellyfin release to run, such as "12.4". On Debian and Ubuntu it pins the jellyfin-server and jellyfin-web packages; on Rocky Linux and Fedora, the tag of the docker.io/jellyfin/jellyfin image.

inputs.name: media_dirs
inputs.description: Directories holding your media, such as ["/srv/media/movies"]. The circuit checks the jellyfin user can read each one and never changes them. On Rocky Linux and Fedora each is mounted read-only into the container at the same path.

inputs.name: port
inputs.description: HTTP port Jellyfin listens on, on every address.

inputs.name: data_dir
inputs.description: Directory for Jellyfin's database, metadata and plugins. On Rocky Linux and Fedora it also holds Jellyfin's configuration and logs, which Debian and Ubuntu keep in /etc/jellyfin and /var/log/jellyfin.

inputs.name: cache_dir
inputs.description: Directory for Jellyfin's cache: transcodes, images and the like. It can grow large.

inputs.name: hardware_acceleration
inputs.description: Let Jellyfin use the host's GPU for transcoding: adds the jellyfin user to the render and video groups and, in the container, passes /dev/dri through when the host has it. Pick the method in Jellyfin's dashboard afterwards.

inputs.name: extra_groups
inputs.description: More groups for the jellyfin user, such as ["media"], so it can read media owned by that group. The groups must exist. The circuit only adds groups, never removes one.

inputs.name: admin_username
inputs.description: Name of the administrator to create in place of Jellyfin's setup wizard. When null, the wizard waits for whoever opens Jellyfin first.

inputs.name: admin_password
inputs.description: Password for admin_username. It reaches the host in a root-only file and never the plan or state.

inputs.name: image_digest
inputs.description: Digest of the image for jellyfin_version, on hosts that run the image. Podman pulls by the digest, so change it with the version.
